note: Rail buttons now guide only while two of them are still in the rail - with two buttons, until the forward one leaves the top. Of the 1,069 design files the app is checked against, 8 carry a rail button and 7 change: the rod-exit speed the report shows falls by a median 48 % on the default 1 m rod, and 26 of their 37 configurations drop below the report's 15 m/s guidance. Enter your rod or rail's real length: the app allows for where the lugs and buttons sit (a new setting, on by default), and a new Rail button starts as an auto-placed pair. Auto (optimal) now works out a delay for every motor mount. Each RockSim simulation flies its own recovery triggers, a .rkt save writes them, and a RockSim motor on a mount that is not there goes to the next free mount of its stage (LOC's Saturn V 5x54 now flies the one motor its file loads, not five). Roll inertia is taken about the rocket's own center of mass. A strap-on booster has its own nozzle exit diameter, and a 0 in a nozzle field now stays off. Seven motor names from RockSim and other files now load the right motor or say why not. Comparison charts put two quantities on one plot, each on its own scale. Each motor mount has its own maximum motor length. Saved runs from before the rail, roll-inertia, strap-on or pod change need a new Launch.
